orderOfOperations.title: Order of Operations
orderOfOperations.description: Evaluate multi-step numeric expressions using the standard order: Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication/Division (left to right), Addition/Subtraction (left to right).

concepts.name: PEMDAS Basics
concepts.explanation: Work parentheses first, then exponents, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right.

concepts.name: Nested Operations & Exponents
concepts.explanation: Exponents are evaluated before multiplication and division. When parentheses are nested, work from the innermost pair outward.

fractions.title: Fractions
fractions.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide fractions, and express answers in lowest terms.

concepts.name: Adding & Subtracting Fractions
concepts.explanation: Fractions need a common denominator before you can add or subtract the numerators. Reduce the result to lowest terms.

concepts.name: Multiplying & Dividing Fractions
concepts.explanation: Multiply fractions straight across (numerator times numerator, denominator times denominator). To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.

decimals.title: Decimals
decimals.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimal numbers.

concepts.name: Adding & Subtracting Decimals
concepts.explanation: Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract as with whole numbers.

concepts.name: Multiplying & Dividing Decimals
concepts.explanation: Multiply as whole numbers, then place the decimal point so the result has as many decimal places as both factors combined. For division, shift decimal points to make the divisor a whole number.

steps: Total decimal places in the factors: \(1 + 1 = 2\)
Shift the decimal point in both numbers by one place: \(64 \div 2\)

percentages.title: Percentages
percentages.description: Find a percent of a number and compute percent change.

concepts.name: Percent of a Number
concepts.explanation: To find P% of a number N, convert the percent to a decimal (divide by 100) and multiply by N.

concepts.name: Percent Change
concepts.explanation: Percent change equals (new minus old) divided by old, times 100. A positive result is an increase; a negative result is a decrease.

examples.problem: A price rises from $40 to $50. Find the percent change.
A price drops from $80 to $60. Find the percent change.

ratiosProportions.title: Ratios & Proportions
ratiosProportions.description: Simplify ratios and solve proportions where two ratios are set equal.

concepts.name: Simplifying Ratios
concepts.explanation: A ratio a:b is simplified by dividing both terms by their greatest common divisor, just like a fraction.

concepts.name: Solving Proportions
concepts.explanation: In a proportion a/b = c/d, cross-multiply (a times d equals b times c) and solve for the missing value.

integers.title: Integers
integers.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide positive and negative whole numbers.

concepts.name: Adding & Subtracting Integers
concepts.explanation: Adding a negative number is the same as subtracting its positive value; subtracting a negative is the same as adding its positive value.

steps: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: \(4 - (-7) = 4 + 7\)

concepts.name: Multiplying & Dividing Integers
concepts.explanation: The product or quotient of two numbers with the same sign is positive; with different signs, it's negative.

steps: Same signs (both negative) means a positive result
Different signs (negative divided by positive) means a negative result

exponentsRoots.title: Exponents & Roots
exponentsRoots.description: Evaluate powers of integers and find square and cube roots.

concepts.name: Evaluating Powers
concepts.explanation: An exponent tells you how many times to multiply the base by itself. A negative base raised to an even power is positive; raised to an odd power, it stays negative.

concepts.name: Square & Cube Roots
concepts.explanation: The square root of n is the number that multiplies by itself to give n. The cube root of n is the number that, cubed, gives n (and can be negative).

steps: Find a number that squares to 49
Find a number that cubes to -27
\((-3)^3 = -27\), so the cube root of -27 is -3
